title: Bacterial RNA polymerase β as an encyclopedia target
dek: Wikipedia's RNA polymerase page is the enzyme. rpoB RRDR alleles and rifamycin plates already own TB DST. Title avoids stealing the rifampin search.
story: Bacterial RNA polymerase on Wikipedia is the multi-subunit enzyme that transcribes DNA. The β subunit (rpoB) is where rifamycins bind. That is the encyclopedia enzyme node.
Simplfy already has tb-rifampin for S450L and friends, tb-xpert-ultra for the cartridge window, and tb-rpoc-compensatory for fitness. This card is the enzyme those alleles live in.
Eukaryotic RNAP Wikipedia trivia is out of scope. Do not dose rifampin from a polymerase article.
deep: RRDR numbering conventions (E. coli versus Mtb) already confuse reports — clinic plate territory.
Silent RRDR SNPs that drop Xpert probes are interpretation, not encyclopedia.
Compensatory rpoC/rpoA alleles are a different plate.
I491F outside the window is marked on the GeneXpert glossary track.

visual.caption: Encyclopedia enzyme, TB-relevant window marked as a pointer to the rifampin plate rather than as a new DST table.
